Definition: from G3947 ("paroxysm"); incitement (to good), or dispute (in anger):--contention, provoke unto.
BiblicalUsage: Paroxysmos is provocation, a sharp contention, an incitement. It cuts both ways: in Acts 15:39 the contention between Paul and Barnabas is so sharp they depart asunder, and in Hebrews 10:24 believers are to provoke one another to love and to good works.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the same sharp edge can split a partnership or sharpen a church, and Hebrews tells me which way to point it: provoke one another to love, not to quarrelling.
